title.zh: 第九 祭祀下 宗廟 社稷 靈星 先農 迎春
title.en: Volume 99: Rituals and Worship Part Three
title.raw: 第九 祭祀下 宗廟 社稷 靈星 先農 迎春 Volume 99: Rituals and Worship Part Three

sentences.zh: 志第九 祭祀下

translations.literal: Treatise Nine: Sacrifices, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 9: Sacrifices, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 宗庙 社稷 灵星 先农 迎春

translations.literal: Ancestral temples; She and Ji; Lingxing; Prior Farmer; welcoming spring.
translations.idiomatic: Topics: ancestral temples; the altars of soil and grain; the Lingxing sacrifice; the god of the first ploughing; the rite that greets spring.

sentences.zh: 光武帝建武二年正月，立高庙于雒阳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu established the shrine to Emperor Gao (Liu Bang) at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianwu 2 (26 CE), Guangwu founded the High Ancestor’s temple in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四时祫祀，高帝为太祖，文帝为太宗，武帝为世宗，如旧。

translations.literal: At the seasonal xi sacrifices and the collective offering, Emperor Gao was honored as Grand Progenitor, Emperor Wen as Grand Exemplar, and Emperor Wu as World Exemplar, as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the four seasonal xi rites and the joint sacrifice, Gao remained Grand Progenitor, Wen the Grand Exemplar, and Wu the World Exemplar—unchanged from earlier practice.

sentences.zh: 余帝四时春以正月，夏以四月，秋以七月，冬以十月及腊，一岁五祀。

translations.literal: For the other emperors, the four seasons were observed in spring in the first month, in summer in the fourth month, in autumn in the seventh month, and in winter in the tenth month and at the year-end la sacrifice—five sacrifices in one year.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining sovereigns were honored five times a year: spring in the first month, summer in the fourth, autumn in the seventh, winter in the tenth, plus the la offering at year’s end.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，立亲庙雒阳，祀父南顿君以上至舂陵节侯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he established private ancestral shrines at Luoyang, sacrificing from his father Lord of Nandun upward to Marquis Jieling of Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 3 he set up shrines to his own line in Luoyang, reaching from his father, the Lord of Nandun, up to the Jieling marquis of Chunling.

sentences.zh: 时寇贼未夷，方务征伐，祀仪未设。

translations.literal: At that time bandits had not yet been pacified, and the court was busy with campaigns, so the full ritual program had not been instituted.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were still active and the state was absorbed in war, so the liturgy of sacrifice had not yet been fixed.

sentences.zh: 至十九年，盗贼讨除，戎事差息，于是五官中郎将张纯与太仆朱浮奏议：「礼，为人子事大宗，降其私亲。

translations.literal: By the nineteenth year the robbers had been eliminated and military affairs had somewhat eased; then Central Court Gentleman-General Zhang Chun and Grand Coachman Zhu Fu submitted a memorial: “According to the Rites, a son who serves the great lineage lowers his private kin.”
translations.idiomatic: By year nineteen the rebels were gone and arms could rest; Zhang Chun and Zhu Fu then argued from the canonical Rites that one who serves the main imperial line must demote one’s private ancestors.

sentences.zh: 礼之设施，不授之与自得之异意。

translations.literal: The setting up of ritual is not a matter of granting it from without versus obtaining it from within—different intentions.”
translations.idiomatic: Whether rites are imposed from above or arise from inner conviction, the principle is not the same.”

sentences.zh: 当除今亲庙四。

translations.literal: The four private shrines now standing should be abolished.”
translations.idiomatic: Four shrines to his immediate forebears should therefore be removed.”

sentences.zh: 孝宣皇以孙后祖，为父立庙于奉明，曰皇考庙，独群臣侍祠。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan, being a grandson who succeeded his grandfather, had built for his father a temple at Fengming called the Temple of the Imperial Father, where only ministers attended the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had raised a “royal father” temple at Fengming for his natural father, served only by officials, because he had inherited from his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 愿下有司议先帝四庙当代亲庙者及皇考庙事。

translations.literal: We ask that the authorities deliberate which four shrines of former emperors should replace the present private shrines, and what to do with the Temple of the Imperial Father.”
translations.idiomatic: They asked the court to decide which four earlier Han shrines should substitute for Guangwu’s private halls, and how to treat the “imperial father” shrine.

sentences.zh: 」下公卿、博士、议郎。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the excellencies, erudits, and deliberation gentlemen.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the question to the three dukes, the academicians, and the deliberation gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 大司徒涉等议：「宜奉所代，立平帝、哀帝、成帝、元帝庙，代今亲庙。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Education Dai She and others argued: “You should honor those you have succeeded by establishing temples to Emperor Ping, Emperor Ai, Emperor Cheng, and Emperor Yuan, in place of the present private shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Dai She’s party said Guangwu should take over the Western Han line by enshrining Ping, Ai, Cheng, and Yuan in place of his own four private temples.

sentences.zh: 兄弟以下，使有司祠。

translations.literal: For brothers and those below, let the relevant offices sacrifice.”
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers and more distant kin could be tended by routine official cults.”

sentences.zh: 宜为南顿君立皇考庙，祭上至舂陵节侯，群臣奉祠。

translations.literal: You should establish a Temple of the Imperial Father for the Lord of Nandun, sacrificing up to the Marquis of Jieling, with ministers attending.”
translations.idiomatic: For his own father they proposed a “royal father” temple from Nandun up to Jieling, with the bureaucracy as celebrants.”

sentences.zh: 」时议有异，不著。

translations.literal: At that time opinions differed, and the dissenting views were not recorded.”
translations.idiomatic: Debate split the court, and the minority positions went unwritten in the record.”

sentences.zh: 上可涉等议，诏曰：「以宗庙处所未定，且礻合祭高庙。

translations.literal: The emperor approved She’s proposal and issued an edict: “Because the sites for the ancestral temples are not yet settled, for now perform the joint sacrifice at the High Temple.”
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu endorsed them but added that, until permanent temple ground was chosen, all would temporarily join the sacrifice at the High Ancestor’s temple.

sentences.zh: 其成、哀、平且祠祭长安故高庙。

translations.literal: For the time being let Cheng, Ai, and Ping be worshipped at the old High Temple in Chang’an.”
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Ai, and Ping would meanwhile receive cult at the former Chang’an High Temple.”

sentences.zh: 其南阳舂陵岁时各且因故园庙祭祀。

translations.literal: Let Nanyang and Chunling each, at the proper seasons, sacrifice for the time being at the old garden shrines.”
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang and Chunling could keep seasonal offerings at their existing garden-temples for the moment.

sentences.zh: 园庙去太守治所远者，在所令长行太守事侍祠。

translations.literal: Where a garden shrine lay far from the prefect’s seat, the magistrate on site should act as prefect and attend the cult.”
translations.idiomatic: If a garden-temple sat beyond easy reach of the prefect, the local magistrate was to stand in for him at the rites.

sentences.zh: 惟孝宣帝有功德，其上尊号曰中宗。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Xiaoxuan, who had true merit and virtue, should receive the posthumous honorific Central Exemplar.”
translations.idiomatic: Xuan alone, for genuine achievement, deserved the title Central Exemplar.”

sentences.zh: 」于是雒阳高庙四时加祭孝宣、孝元，凡五帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon at Luoyang’s High Temple the four seasonal rites added sacrifices to Xuan and Yuan, making five emperors in all.”
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang’s High Temple then honored five sovereigns in the seasonal round, adding Xuan and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 其西庙成、哀、平三帝主，四时祭于故高庙。

translations.literal: The western temple housed the spirit tablets of Cheng, Ai, and Ping, with seasonal sacrifice at the old High Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The western hall kept the tablets of Cheng, Ai, and Ping, served at the old High Temple each season.

sentences.zh: 东庙，京兆尹侍祠，冠衣车服如太常祠陵庙之礼。

translations.literal: The eastern temple was tended by the Governor of the Capital, with caps, robes, chariots, and equipage like those used when the Chamberlain for Ceremonial tended imperial tombs.”
translations.idiomatic: The eastern hall fell to the metropolitan governor, who matched the Chamberlain’s tomb ritual in dress and equipage.

sentences.zh: 南顿君以上至节侯，皆就园庙。

translations.literal: From the Lord of Nandun up to Marquis Jieling, all cult was returned to the garden shrines.”
translations.idiomatic: The line from Nandun through Jieling was worshipped only at the garden-temples.

sentences.zh: 南顿君称皇考庙，钜鹿都尉称皇祖考庙，郁林太守称皇曾祖考庙，节侯称皇高祖考庙，在所郡县侍祠。

translations.literal: The Lord of Nandun was titled Temple of the Imperial Father, the Commandant of Julu Temple of the Imperial Grandfather, the Governor of Yulin Temple of the Imperial Great-Grandfather, and Marquis Jieling Temple of the Imperial High-Great-Grandfather; the counties where they lay supplied the attendants.”
translations.idiomatic: Each forebear received a graded “royal ancestor” title—father, grandfather, great-grandfather, and earliest known ancestor—with county officials conducting the rites.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，有诏问张纯，禘礻合之礼不施行几年。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year an edict asked Zhang Chun how many years it had been since the di and xia joint rites had last been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six the court questioned Zhang Chun on how long the grand di and xia offerings had been suspended.

sentences.zh: 纯奏：「礼，三年一祫，五年一禘。

translations.literal: Chun submitted: “The Rites prescribe a collective xi every three years and a di every five years.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun replied that canon called for a xi every three years and a di every five.

sentences.zh: 毁庙之主，陈于太祖；

translations.literal: Spirits from destroyed shrines are arrayed before the Grand Progenitor.”
translations.idiomatic: Tablets from abolished temples were brought before the first ancestor.

sentences.zh: 未毁庙之主，皆升，合食太祖；

translations.literal: Spirits from shrines not yet destroyed all ascend and share a meal with the Grand Progenitor.”
translations.idiomatic: Tablets of still-standing temples likewise ascended to feast with the founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 五年再殷察。

translations.literal: Within five years the grand Yin sacrifices are performed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual canon calls for two great Yin offerings within each five-year span; received editions vary this line.

sentences.zh: 旧制，三年三祫，毁庙主合食高庙，存庙主未尝合。

translations.literal: Under the old Han system there were three xi in three years: tablets from destroyed temples joined Gao’s meal, while tablets from surviving temples had never joined in one meal.
translations.idiomatic: Former practice held three xi in three years: only spirits from razed shrines ate with Gao; standing temples had not yet been merged.

sentences.zh: 元始五年，始行禘礼。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Yuanshi era the di rite was first performed.
translations.idiomatic: The di was first enacted in Yuanshi 5 (5 CE).

sentences.zh: 父为昭，南向；

translations.literal: Fathers occupy the zhao (south-facing) side.”
translations.idiomatic: Fathers stood on the zhao, the southern file.

sentences.zh: 子为穆，北向。

translations.literal: Sons occupy the mu (north-facing) side.”
translations.idiomatic: Sons stood on the mu, facing north.

sentences.zh: 父子不并坐，而孙从王父。

translations.literal: Father and son do not sit side by side; grandsons follow their grandfather’s file.”
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were not paired in the same row; grandsons aligned under the grandfather’s column.

sentences.zh: 禘之为言谛，禘諟昭穆，尊卑之义。

translations.literal: The word di means ‘to make clear’; the di sorts zhao and mu and fixes the meaning of high and low.”
translations.idiomatic: Di means “discernment”: it sets zhao and mu and thereby rank.

sentences.zh: 以夏四月阳气在上，阴气在下，故正尊卑之义。

translations.literal: Because in the fourth month of summer the yang ether is above and the yin below, it rectifies the meaning of precedence.”
translations.idiomatic: Held in the fourth month, when yang rides high and yin lies below, it expresses who is senior and who junior.

sentences.zh: 礻合以冬十月，五谷成熟，故骨肉合饮食。

translations.literal: The xia takes place in the tenth month of winter, when the five grains are ripe, so bone and flesh share a common meal.”
translations.idiomatic: The winter xia in the tenth month, when grain is gathered, gathers the lineage for a communal meal with the dead.

sentences.zh: 祖宗庙未定，且合祭。

translations.literal: Because the shrines of the founding ancestors are not yet fixed, for now perform only the joint sacrifice.”
translations.idiomatic: Until the founding temples were settled, only the combined offering was used.

sentences.zh: 今宜以时定。

translations.literal: Now it should be fixed in due course.”
translations.idiomatic: The time had come to settle the schedule in law.

sentences.zh: 」语在《纯传》。

translations.literal: The account is given in Zhang Chun’s biography.”
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in Zhang Chun’s biography.

sentences.zh: 上难复立庙，遂以合祭高庙为常。

translations.literal: The emperor found it hard to rebuild separate temples, so he made the joint sacrifice at the High Temple the standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu kept rebuilding separate halls impracticable, so the collective offering at the High Temple became the norm.

sentences.zh: 后以三年冬祫，五年夏禘之时，但就陈祭毁庙主而已，谓之殷。

translations.literal: Later, at the winter xi of the third year and the summer di of the fifth year, they merely set out and sacrificed the tablets from destroyed shrines—this was called the Yin offering.”
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, at the third year’s winter xi and the fifth year’s summer di, only tablets from dismantled shrines were brought out—the so-called Yin rite.

sentences.zh: 太祖东面，惠、文、武、元帝为昭，景、宣帝为穆。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor faced east; Emperors Hui, Wen, Wu, and Yuan formed the zhao file; Emperors Jing and Xuan the mu file.
translations.idiomatic: The founding ancestor faced east; Hui, Wen, Wu, and Yuan were zhao; Jing and Xuan were mu.

sentences.zh: 惠、景、昭三帝非殷祭时不祭。

translations.literal: The three emperors Hui, Jing, and Zhao received no sacrifice except at these grand Yin rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, Jing, and Zhao were omitted from ordinary seasonal cult and appeared only at the grand Yin.

sentences.zh: 光武皇帝崩，明帝即位，以光武帝拨乱中兴，更为起庙，尊号曰世祖庙。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu died and Emperor Ming succeeded, because Guangwu had quelled chaos and restored the dynasty, a new temple was built for him with the honorific title Shrine of the World Exemplar.”
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi, crediting Guangwu with restoring the house, raised a new temple titled Shrine of the World Exemplar.

sentences.zh: 以元帝于光武为穆，故虽非宗，不毁也。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Yuan stood in the mu column relative to Guangwu, although he was not counted a “exemplar” shrine, his temple was not destroyed.”
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, though not a “numbered” exemplar, stayed on the mu side opposite Guangwu and so escaped abolition.

sentences.zh: 后遂为常。

translations.literal: This later became fixed practice.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement then stayed permanent.

sentences.zh: 古不墓祭，汉诸陵皆有园寝，承秦所为也。

translations.literal: Antiquity did not sacrifice at tombs; every Han imperial tomb had a garden lodge—this followed Qin usage.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients did not worship at graves; Han mausolea gained garden-palaces, a Qin habit carried over.

sentences.zh: 说者以为古宗庙前制庙，后制寝，以象人之居前有朝，后有寝也。

translations.literal: Expositors hold that in high antiquity an ancestral temple had a shrine in front and a sleeping chamber behind, matching a living person’s front hall and rear chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars say the classic temple placed the hall of tablets in front and a “sleeping” chamber behind, like a ruler’s court and private quarters.

sentences.zh: 《月令》有「先荐寝庙」，《诗》称「寝庙弈弈」，言相通也。

translations.literal: The ‘Monthly Ordinances’ speaks of ‘first offering in the sleeping chamber and temple,’ and the Odes praise ‘sleeping chamber and temple, stately and bright,’ meaning the two communicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances and the Book of Odes treat shrine and rear chamber as linked spaces.

sentences.zh: 庙以藏主，以四时祭。

translations.literal: The temple housed the tablets and received the four seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The frontal temple kept spirit tablets and took the quarterly offerings.

sentences.zh: 寝有衣冠几杖象生之具，以荐新物。

translations.literal: The sleeping chamber held caps, robes, staffs, and implements as if the dead were alive, for presenting new produce.
translations.idiomatic: The rear chamber displayed grave goods and received first-fruits as though the sovereign still lived.

sentences.zh: 秦始出寝，起于墓侧，汉因而弗改，故陵上称寝殿，起居衣服象生人之具，古寝之意也。

translations.literal: Qin first moved the sleeping chamber out to the side of the tomb; Han continued without change, so the ridge hall is called the sleeping palace—daily dress and gear imitate the living; this preserves the idea of the ancient rear chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Qin relocated the “sleeping” cult beside the mound; Han kept it, hence “sleeping halls” on the tumulus furnished like living quarters.

sentences.zh: 建武以来，关西诸陵以转久远，但四时特牲祠；

translations.literal: Since the rise of Jianwu, the western Guanzhong tombs, being very old, received only a special victim each season.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianwu, distant tombs in the west got a single seasonal victim each.

sentences.zh: 帝每幸长安谒诸陵，乃太牢祠。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor visited Chang’an and paid his respects at the tombs, then a full tai-lao was offered.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the sovereign toured Chang’an and called at the mausolea was a full tai-lao slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 自雒阳诸陵至灵帝，皆以晦望二十四气伏腊及四时祠。

translations.literal: From the Luoyang tombs down to Lingdi, sacrifice fell on the dark and bright moons, the twenty-four qi nodes, the fu and la festivals, and the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang-area tombs through Lingdi were served at new and full moon, the solar terms, fu and la, and the quarterly round.

sentences.zh: 庙日上饭，太官送用物，园令、食监典省，其亲陵所宫人随鼓漏理被枕，具盥水，陈严具。

translations.literal: On temple days food was sent up; the Grand Provisioner supplied the goods; the park superintendent and the food intendant inspected; at mausolea the palace women followed the clepsydra to arrange bedding and pillows, set out wash-water, and array the grave goods.
translations.idiomatic: Temple days meant sending meals from the imperial kitchen, with park wardens checking gear while palace women, timing by water-clock, made beds, poured water, and laid out grave goods at the ruler’s own tomb.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，立太社稷于雒阳，在宗庙之右，方坛，无屋，有墙门而已。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu the Grand altars of She and Ji were founded east of Luoyang, to the right of the ancestral temples—square earthen platforms without roofs, only a walled gateway.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 2 saw the great altars of soil and grain east of Luoyang, south of the temples—open-air square mounds with a gate.

sentences.zh: 二月、八月及腊，一岁三祠，皆太牢具，使有司祠。

translations.literal: In the second and eighth months and at la, three sacrifices a year, all used a full tai-lao and were performed by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: They were offered three times yearly—second month, eighth month, and la—with tai-lao victims under commissioned officials.

sentences.zh: 《孝经援神契》曰：「社者，土地之主也。

translations.literal: The ‘Classic of Filial Piety, Assorted Proofs of the Spirits’ says: ‘She is the lord of the land.
translations.idiomatic: The Apocrypha to the Classic of Filial Piety states: She is master of the soil.

sentences.zh: 稷者，五谷之长也。

translations.literal: Ji is the chief of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Ji is chief among the five grains.

sentences.zh: 」《礼记》及《国语》皆谓共工氏之子曰句龙，为后土官，能平九土，故祀以为社。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites and the Discourses of the States both say that Gonggong’s son Goulong, as minister of earth, could level the nine soils, and therefore was worshipped as She.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites and Guoyu name Goulong, son of Gonggong, earth officer who levelled the nine domains, and therefore deified as She.

sentences.zh: 烈山氏之子曰柱，能植百谷疏，自夏以上祀以为稷，至殷以柱久远，而尧时弃为后稷，亦植百谷，故废柱，祀弃为稷。

translations.literal: The son of the Lie Mountain clan was named Zhu; he could plant the hundred grains and vegetables; from Xia upward he was worshipped as Ji; by Yin, Zhu being remote, and Qi of Yao’s time having become Minister of Millet and likewise able to plant the hundred grains, Zhu was abolished and Qi was worshipped as Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lie Mountain’s son Zhu, who grew every crop, had been Ji until Yin times; then Qi, Yao’s Minister of Millet, replaced the obsolete Zhu.

sentences.zh: 大司农郑玄说，古者官有大功，则配食其神。

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Zheng Xuan explains that when an ancient office achieved great merit, it shared sacrifice with the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan notes that great offices “ate beside” the gods they served.

sentences.zh: 故句龙配食于社，弃配食于稷。

translations.literal: Therefore Goulong shares She’s offering and Qi shares Ji’s offering.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Goulong is paired with She and Qi with Ji.

sentences.zh: 郡县置社稷，太守、令、长侍祠，牲用羊□。

translations.literal: In commanderies and counties She and Ji were set up; the prefect or magistrate attended; the victim was sheep [character missing in text].
translations.idiomatic: County altars were served by prefect or magistrate with sheep (the text has a lacuna after “sheep”).

sentences.zh: 唯州所治有社无稷，以其使官。

translations.literal: Only at the seat of a province was there She without Ji, because the inspector was a roaming official.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial seats had soil but not grain, since the inspector was not a resident magistrate.

sentences.zh: 古者师行平有载社主，不载稷也。

translations.literal: Anciently when armies marched, always they carried the She spirit tablet; they did not carry Ji (the text reads 师行平有, likely 师行必有).
translations.idiomatic: On campaign armies bore the earth tablet but not that of grain—an ancient rule (the received text is corrupt at “always”).

sentences.zh: 国家亦有五祀之祭，有司掌之，其礼简于社稷云。

translations.literal: The state also maintained cult of the five household spirits; offices managed it, and the rite was simpler than for She and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Han additionally kept the five domestic sacrifices under bureaus, with lighter ritual than the great altars.

sentences.zh: 汉兴八年，有言周兴而邑立后稷之祀，于是高帝令天下立灵星祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year after the founding of Han someone said that when Zhou rose it founded sacrifice to Hou Ji in the capital; therefore Gaozu ordered She altars named Lingxing established empire-wide.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s eighth year saw a memorial likening Zhou’s capital cult of Hou Ji to Han’s need; Gaozu then ordered Lingxing shrines throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 言祠后稷而谓之灵星者，以后稷又配食星也。

translations.literal: The reason the sacrifice to Hou Ji was called Lingxing is that Hou Ji also received paired worship with a constellation.
translations.idiomatic: The name Lingxing (“spirit star”) attached to Hou Ji because he shared offerings with a star.

sentences.zh: 旧说，星谓天田星也。

translations.literal: Old glosses identify the star as the “heavenly field” star.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition equates that star with the celestial field.

sentences.zh: 一曰，龙左角为天田官，主谷。

translations.literal: Another view: the dragon’s left horn is the office of the heavenly field and governs grain.
translations.idiomatic: Another opinion makes the dragon’s left horn the celestial granary.

sentences.zh: 祀用壬辰位祠之。

translations.literal: The cult uses the stem ren and branch chen position.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice was oriented to the ren-chen alignment.

sentences.zh: 壬为水，辰为龙，就其类也。

translations.literal: Ren belongs to water and chen to the dragon; one chooses its kindred element.
translations.idiomatic: Water (ren) and the dragon (chen) were paired by sympathetic category.

sentences.zh: 牲用太牢，县邑令长侍祠。

translations.literal: The victim was a full tai-lao; county magistrates attended.
translations.idiomatic: Victims were tai-lao; county magistrates presided.

sentences.zh: 舞者用童男十六人。

translations.literal: The dancers were sixteen boys.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen boy dancers performed.

sentences.zh: 舞者象教田，初为芟除，次耕种、芸耨、驱爵及获刈、舂簸之形，象其功也。

translations.literal: The dance mimicked teaching fieldwork: first clearing brush, then ploughing, weeding, chasing sparrows, reaping, threshing, and winnowing—acting out the whole labor.
translations.idiomatic: Their dance enacted the farming year—slash, plough, hoe, shoo birds, reap, pound, and winnow.

sentences.zh: 县邑常以乙未日祠先农于乙地，以丙戌日祠风伯于戌地，以己丑日祠雨师于丑地，用羊□。

translations.literal: Districts and towns regularly sacrificed to the Prior Farmer on a yiwei day at yi ground, to the Wind Lord on a bingxu day at xu ground, and to the Lord of Rain on a jichou day at chou ground, using sheep [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Localities offered to the first plough on yiwei at “yi” soil, to the wind god on bingxu at xu, and to the rain master on jichou at chou, with sheep (text damaged).

sentences.zh: 立春之日，皆青幡帻，迎春于东郭外。

translations.literal: On the day Establishing Spring everyone wore green headcloths and greeted spring outside the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the Beginning of Spring the court donned green kerchiefs and welcomed the season beyond the eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 令一童男冒青巾，衣青衣，先在东郭外野中。

translations.literal: A single boy was wrapped in a green scarf and dressed in green and stationed beforehand in the open east of the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: One boy in green waited in the wilds east of the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 迎春至者，自野中出，则迎者拜之而还，弗祭。

translations.literal: When the spring-welcoming party arrived and he came out of the wilds, the greeters bowed to him and returned—there was no further sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The procession met him, bowed, and went home without an altar service.

sentences.zh: 三时不迎。

translations.literal: The other three seasons were not greeted in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, autumn, and winter had no parallel rite.

sentences.zh: 论曰：「臧文仲祀爰居，而孔子以为不知。

translations.literal: The essayist remarks: “Zang Wenzhong sacrificed to the seabird Yuanju, and Confucius thought him ignorant.”
translations.idiomatic: The commentary opens: Zang Wenzhong’s cult to the Yuanju bird drew Confucius’s rebuke for ignorance.

sentences.zh: 《汉书·郊祀志》著自秦以来迄于王莽，典祀或有未修，而爰居之类众焉。

translations.literal: The ‘Han Treatise on Suburban and Other Sacrifices’ records from Qin down to Wang Mang: some canonical cults were neglected, while oddities like Yuanju multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Han treatise shows how irregular cults piled up from Qin through Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 世祖中兴，蠲除非常，修复旧祀，方之前事邈殊矣。

translations.literal: Our Founding Emperor restored the middle and cut away the abnormal, repairing old sacrifices—how far that is from the earlier tangle!
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu’s restoration scrapped the exotic and revived the old rites—a world away from the past.

sentences.zh: 尝闻儒言，三皇无文，结绳以治，自五帝始有书契。

translations.literal: I once heard scholars say that the Three August Ones left no writing and governed by knotted cords; writing and contracts begin with the Five Thearchs.
translations.idiomatic: Confucians say the Three Sovereigns had no script and used knotted cords; records begin with the Five Thearchs.

sentences.zh: 至于三王，俗化雕文，诈伪渐兴，始有印玺，以检奸萌，然犹未有金玉银铜之器也。

translations.literal: By the Three Kings custom had carved patterns, deceit gradually arose, and seals first appeared to check treachery—yet there were still no vessels of gold, jade, silver, or copper.
translations.idiomatic: Under the three dynasties ornament and fraud grew; seals curbed malice, but precious metal ware did not yet exist.

sentences.zh: 自上皇以来封泰山者，至周七十二代。

translations.literal: From high antiquity those who feng Mount Tai down to Zhou number seventy-two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two generations from remote antiquity through Zhou are said to have performed the Tai feng.

sentences.zh: 封者，谓封土为坛，柴祭告天，代兴成功也。

translations.literal: Feng means piling earth into an altar, burning firewood to announce to Heaven that a new age has succeeded and its work is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Feng meant raising a mound and burning the report that a new mandate had fulfilled its task.

sentences.zh: 《礼记》所谓「因名山升中于天」者也。

translations.literal: This is what the Book of Rites calls ‘by a famous mountain ascending and reporting in the middle of Heaven.’
translations.idiomatic: It matches the Rites: “By a famed peak ascend and report to Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 易姓则改封者，著一代之始，明不相袭也。

translations.literal: When the surname of the ruling house changes, the feng is altered, to mark the beginning of a new age and show that one does not simply inherit the former rite.
translations.idiomatic: A change of dynasty required a new feng to signal a fresh mandate, not a mere copy of the old.

sentences.zh: 继世之王巡狩，则修封以祭而已。

translations.literal: Later kings on tour merely repaired the feng and sacrificed—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Later sovereigns on inspection tours only refurbished the altar and offered sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自秦始皇、孝武帝封泰山，本由好仙、信方士之言，造为石检印封之事也。

translations.literal: From the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han, the feng on Mount Tai arose from love of immortality and trust in fangshi talk, producing the business of stone casings and sealed imprints.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi climbed Tai out of quest for immortals and occultists’ tales, hence stone caskets and sealed credentials.

sentences.zh: 所闻如此。

translations.literal: What I have heard is like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the tradition I have heard.

sentences.zh: 虽诚天道难可度知，然其大较犹有本要。

translations.literal: Although the Way of Heaven is hard to measure, its general outline still has a root principle.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s way may be unfathomable, yet its broad pattern has an intelligible basis.

sentences.zh: 天道质诚，约而不费者也。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is plain and sincere—economical and free of waste.”
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s way is simple and true—spare and without extravagance.”

sentences.zh: 故牲有犊，器用陶匏，殆将无事于检封之间，而乐难攻之石也。

translations.literal: Therefore the victims were calves, and the vessels were pottery and gourd—probably nothing to do with the business of stone casings and sealing, yet they delighted in attacking those stones.
translations.idiomatic: So the rites used young calves and plain earthenware and gourds—far from the stone-casket sealing fad—yet rulers still took perverse pleasure in smashing those rocks.

sentences.zh: 且唯封为改代，故曰岱宗。

translations.literal: Moreover it is only the feng that marks a change of mandate; hence Mount Dai is called the Exalted Peak of the Lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Tai feng announces a new mandate, which is why Mount Dai is called the Ancestral Peak.

sentences.zh: 夏康、周宣，由废复兴，不闻改封。

translations.literal: Xia Kang and King Xuan of Zhou restored their houses after ruin; one never hears that they altered the feng.
translations.idiomatic: Xia’s Kang and Zhou’s Xuan revived ruined dynasties without redoing the Tai rite.

sentences.zh: 世祖欲因孝武故封，实继祖宗之道也。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor wished to follow Emperor Wu’s old feng in substance, truly continuing the way of the founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu meant to repeat Wudi’s climb in spirit, inheriting the founders’ path.

sentences.zh: 而梁松固争，以为必改。

translations.literal: Yet Liang Song stubbornly argued that the rite must be changed.
translations.idiomatic: But Liang Song insisted the ceremony had to be reinvented.

sentences.zh: 乃当夫既封之后，未有福，而松卒被诛死。

translations.literal: Then, after the feng had already been performed, no blessing appeared, and Song soon met execution.
translations.idiomatic: After the deed was done heaven sent no favor, and Song himself died under the headsman’s blade.

sentences.zh: 虽罪由身，盖亦诬神之咎也。

translations.literal: Although his guilt was personal, it was also the retribution of having insulted the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His crimes were his own, yet they also look like punishment for profaning the gods.

sentences.zh: 且帝王所以能大显于后者，实在其德加于民，不闻其在封矣。

translations.literal: Moreover what enables an emperor to shine brightly to posterity lies truly in his virtue spreading among the people, not in whether he performs the feng.
translations.idiomatic: What makes a ruler remembered is virtue among the living, not a mound on Tai.

sentences.zh: 言天地者莫大于《易》，《易》无六宗在中之象。

translations.literal: Of all who speak of Heaven and Earth none is greater than the Book of Changes, and the Changes shows no image of the Six Ancestors standing between them.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Changes, supreme discourse on Heaven and Earth, nowhere pictures the Six Ancestors sandwiched between them.

sentences.zh: 若信为天地四方所宗，是至大也。

translations.literal: If they are truly to be venerated as what Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters take as their ancestors, that would make them supremely great.
translations.idiomatic: To treat them as the supreme foci of heaven, earth, and the four directions would elevate them beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 而比太社，又为失所，难以为诚矣！

translations.literal: Yet to rank them beside the Grand Altar of Soil is again misplaced; it is hard to call such a scheme sincere!
translations.idiomatic: Pairing them with the great altar of soil only misplaces them further—hardly a credible cult.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：天地禋郊，宗庙享祀，咸秩无文，山川具止。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Heaven and Earth received burnt-offering at the suburban altars; the ancestral temples enjoyed their feasts; every rank received its due though unwritten; mountains and rivers each had their station.
translations.idiomatic: The summation runs: suburban smoke for Heaven and Earth, feasts in the temples, every spirit given its place though unrecorded in full detail, mountains and rivers each assigned.

sentences.zh: 淫乃国紊，典惟皇纪。

translations.literal: Excess throws the state into confusion; the canon is the sovereign’s tether.
translations.idiomatic: Licentious cults disorder the realm; the classical pattern is the emperor’s anchor.

sentences.zh: 肇自盛敬，孰崖厥始？

translations.literal: From utmost reverence in the beginning—who can trace the first cliff of that ascent?
translations.idiomatic: Reverence was there at the start—but who can mark the first step of that height?
